title: Microsoft Teams: customise the file types blocked by Weaponizable File Protection
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned rollout from the PowerShell controls already documented on Microsoft Learn. Its defaults, update behaviour and rollout dates match Microsoft's notice, and targeted searches found no documentation resolving the licensing or admin-centre customisation gaps.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams cmdlet Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration supports -FileTypeCustomizationSetting CustomBlockList -FileTypeBlockList <string[]> for the tenant custom list.
claims.quote: CustomBlockList: Blocks the file types you specify in the FileTypeBlockList parameter instead of the Microsoft-recommended list.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCustomizationSetting MicrosoftRecommendedBlockList restores the recommended list.
claims.quote: MicrosoftRecommendedBlockList: Blocks the file types on the Microsoft-recommended list. This keeps the existing behavior.

claims.claim: The protection switch is in Teams admin center > Messaging settings > Messaging safety > Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Messaging settings.
3. Scroll down to Messaging safety settings.
4. Turn on the setting: Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration with -FileTypeCheck Enabled or Disabled and -Identity Global switches protection on or off rather than selecting extensions.
claims.quote:
Turn off or turn on file protection through PowerShell

You can also configure file protection using PowerShell with the Teams module:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck "Enabled" -Identity Global
